title: feat(status-pages): status edge Worker and renderers

summaries.body:
## Maple review 🟡 **Confidence 5/10** · needs attention Kept at 5: ordinary warnings and soft signals never read below 5. 4 warnings −4 · tests partial −1 · risk medium · 0/2 new units observable −1 · floor 5 Adds an edge Worker and renderer package serving status pages, badges, Atom feeds and summary JSON from KV, R2 and the colo cache, plus break-glass writes straight to KV. Escaping, routing and the token check hold up; three real defects and a vacuous test need attention. None of the listed `HttpClientError`/`NotFoundError` issues is addressed: they come from maple-web's resource bundle, not this diff. - `apps/status` Worker serves `/s/` and host pages from edge storage only - `break-glass` posts per-entry KV updates behind a hashed token and rate limit - `readThrough` falls back cache → KV → R2 → any-age cache with a 503 on outage - `@maple/status-page` renders HTML, `status.json`, Atom and SVG from one snapshot ### Before merge - [ ] **Infra** · Check every environment has what this config now expects · [`alchemy.run.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/0a05d19a862787f4e15cbc63ec2fdd23130b0427/alchemy.run.ts) - [ ] **Manual** · Decide the public hostname for the `status` Worker; today `workersDev: true` only exposes it on workers.dev ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F1 · rememberOverlay call drops cached entries a lagging KV list has not returned correctness · [`apps/status/src/break-glass.ts:192`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/0a05d19a862787f4e15cbc63ec2fdd23130b0427/apps/status/src/break-glass.ts#L192) `rememberOverlay` is called without `previous`, which defaults to `[]` (`snapshot.ts:179`), so the cached overlay is rewritten from the lagging `list` plus the new entry only. Post A caches `[A]`; a second post within the 120s `LIST_LAG_MS` window lists `[]` and caches `[B]`, so A's update disappears from the page visitors see even though both entries are in KV — and `loadOverlay` then keeps serving that cache for up to `OVERLAY_CACHE_FRESH_MS`. This contradicts the comment two lines up and the `previous` handling `loadOverlay` already does at `snapshot.ts:196`. ``` Export `readCachedOverlay` from `snapshot.ts` (or add a `cachedOverlayEntries(env, pageId)` helper) and pass its entries as the fourth argument, as `loadOverlay` does. ```
🟠 Warning · F2 · The status Worker exports no telemetry and opens no span observability · SPAN-01 · [`apps/status/src/worker.ts:45`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/0a05d19a862787f4e15cbc63ec2fdd23130b0427/apps/status/src/worker.ts#L45) `fetch` has no `Effect.withSpan` and the props add no `selfObservabilityEnv`, unlike every other Maple Worker (`apps/alerting/src/worker.ts:61`), so the service never appears in Maple. When KV and R2 both fail the request still answers a plain 503 (`handler.ts:148`, `handler.ts:151`) with the storage error discarded by `Effect.orElseSucceed` (`snapshot.ts:67`, `snapshot.ts:88`), so an outage of the page that exists for outages is invisible: no trace, no log, nothing to alert on. ``` Wire `selfObservabilityEnv(stage, region)` into the Worker props and wrap the `fetch` effect in `Effect.withSpan("status.request", { attributes: { "maple.status.page_id": ..., "maple.status.response_status": ... } })`; export through ingest as the other Workers do. ```
🟠 Warning · F3 · Status select offers statuses the target's kind rejects with a 400 correctness · [`packages/status-page/src/manage.ts:63`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/0a05d19a862787f4e15cbc63ec2fdd23130b0427/packages/status-page/src/manage.ts#L63) The select lists all seven `StatusPageIncidentStatus` values, but `statusFitsKind` (`packages/domain/src/status-page.ts:151`) splits them into incident and maintenance lifecycles, and `break-glass.ts:152` rejects a mismatch. Picking "In progress" for the default "New incident", or "Investigating" for a maintenance listed at `manage.ts:61`, always fails with "That status is for maintenance; pick an incident status." — during an outage the form offers three options that cannot be posted. ``` Render the options per target kind: split the incident `

> [!WARNING]
> **`rememberOverlay` call drops cached entries a lagging KV list has not returned**
>
> <sub>F1 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`rememberOverlay` is called without `previous`, which defaults to `[]` (`snapshot.ts:179`), so the cached overlay is rewritten from the lagging `list` plus the new entry only. Post A caches `[A]`; a second post within the 120s `LIST_LAG_MS` window lists `[]` and caches `[B]`, so A's update disappears from the page visitors see even though both entries are in KV — and `loadOverlay` then keeps serving that cache for up to `OVERLAY_CACHE_FRESH_MS`. This contradicts the comment two lines up and the `previous` handling `loadOverlay` already does at `snapshot.ts:196`.

```
Export `readCachedOverlay` from `snapshot.ts` (or add a `cachedOverlayEntries(env, pageId)` helper) and pass its entries as the fourth argument, as `loadOverlay` does.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **The status Worker exports no telemetry and opens no span**
>
> <sub>F2 · Warning · observability · SPAN-01</sub>

`fetch` has no `Effect.withSpan` and the props add no `selfObservabilityEnv`, unlike every other Maple Worker (`apps/alerting/src/worker.ts:61`), so the service never appears in Maple. When KV and R2 both fail the request still answers a plain 503 (`handler.ts:148`, `handler.ts:151`) with the storage error discarded by `Effect.orElseSucceed` (`snapshot.ts:67`, `snapshot.ts:88`), so an outage of the page that exists for outages is invisible: no trace, no log, nothing to alert on.

```
Wire `selfObservabilityEnv(stage, region)` into the Worker props and wrap the `fetch` effect in `Effect.withSpan("status.request", { attributes: { "maple.status.page_id": ..., "maple.status.response_status": ... } })`; export through ingest as the other Workers do.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Status select offers statuses the target's kind rejects with a 400**
>
> <sub>F3 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The select lists all seven `StatusPageIncidentStatus` values, but `statusFitsKind` (`packages/domain/src/status-page.ts:151`) splits them into incident and maintenance lifecycles, and `break-glass.ts:152` rejects a mismatch. Picking "In progress" for the default "New incident", or "Investigating" for a maintenance listed at `manage.ts:61`, always fails with "That status is for maintenance; pick an incident status." — during an outage the form offers three options that cannot be posted.

```
Render the options per target kind: split the incident `<select>` into incident and maintenance groups (e.g. `<optgroup>` filtered by `INCIDENT_STATUSES`/`MAINTENANCE_STATUSES`), and offer only incident statuses for "New incident".
```

> [!WARNING]
> **The hidden-uptime test cannot fail for the guard it names**
>
> <sub>F4 · Warning · tests</sub>

`fixtureComponentId(2)` is built with `days: []` (`fixtures.ts:93`), so `renderBars` returns "" at the `component.days.length === 0` guard (`page.ts:57`) before `!component.showUptime` is ever consulted. Deleting the `showUptime` check leaves this test green, so the feature is unverified.

```
Build the hidden component with `makeDays(FIXTURE_NOW)` and `showUptime: false` in the test's own snapshot (rather than reusing fixture 2), assert zero bars, and add a `showUptime: true` control with the same days asserting 90.
```
